auth_ext.decode_purpose_token: `payload = None` initialised before try; final `if not payload or payload.get('purpose') != expected_purpose` guard is dead-code for successful jwt.decode (never returns falsy) but is a safe defensive belt — behavior unchanged, still returns HTTPException(400, 'Invalid token purpose') as expected by tests

billing.create_order: new `if not order or 'id' not in order: raise HTTPException(500, 'Razorpay did not return a valid order')` sits AFTER the try/except, so placeholder-key auth failure still surfaces as 'Razorpay error: Authentication failed' via the existing except branch — the new guard only fires if the SDK ever returns an unexpected shape (never in current test env)
critical_code_review_comments: auth_ext.decode_purpose_token: after the try/except, both `jwt.ExpiredSignatureError` and `jwt.PyJWTError` already raise HTTPException — so `payload` can only ever be a dict at line 54. The `if not payload` guard is unreachable in practice. It is harmless (satisfies linters/static analyzers) but a small clarifying comment ('defensive; unreachable in normal flow') would help future maintainers.

billing.create_order: the new `if not order or 'id' not in order` guard is correctly placed AFTER the try/except and only fires if Razorpay returns a truthy-but-malformed object. razorpay-python typically raises on any non-2xx, so this is defensive-only. No test coverage for this branch exists — could add a mocked-client test that returns `{}` from client.order.create if strict coverage matters (low priority).

Frontend files (AuthContext.jsx useMemo, Chat.jsx / billing.js console.warn) were NOT tested in this pass since scope is backend-only per request. useMemo addition is trivial and safe; console.warn on empty catches is strictly additive. Recommend a quick manual smoke test of the login and chat streaming pages when the frontend is retested.

Rebrand appears complete based on strict .py/.jsx grep. Did not grep other extensions (.md, .json, .html, .txt, package.json name field, etc.) — main agent should confirm those separately if branding hygiene matters there too.
test_credentials: Per-file X-Forwarded-For isolation via /app/backend/tests/conftest.py. Ephemeral users created per test class (prefix rt-, cleaned up in teardown). JWT_SECRET from /app/backend/.env used to craft verify/reset tokens in test_auth_ext.py.
seed_data_creation: None new. Existing per-test users and db.payments seed rows are created and cleaned by the test fixtures themselves.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The `if not payload` branch in auth_ext.decode_purpose_token is defensive/unreachable — do not write a test that expects it to fire in normal jwt operation. Similarly, `if not order or 'id' not in order` in billing.create_order will not trip against the placeholder Razorpay keys because the SDK raises before the assignment; testing it requires monkeypatching client.order.create. Rate-limiter is process-local; if you add new rate-limited tests, either use conftest XFF or set your own XFF header (see TestLoginRateLimit pattern). To reset all buckets: `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`. Full run: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v --tb=short --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_next.xml` (~30s).
